title: streaming: add robust lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect/reconnect resume, and server timeouts (OpenAI compat)
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds stable streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel semantics, disconnect/reconnect resume via resume_token, and configurable server-side idle/request timeouts. Backwards compatible OpenAI-compat layer updates included.
description: Motivation: Streaming clients are fragile in the presence of network blips and client-side cancellations. We've seen customer incidents where partial outputs were not resumable, server resources were held by abandoned streams, or OpenAI-compatible clients observed inconsistent behaviors. This PR implements a coherent lifecycle for streaming RPCs across the runtime and OpenAI compatibility proxy. Key changes: 1) Client cancel semantics: Expose explicit 'client_cancel' signal in the streaming protocol. When received, the server now marks the stream terminal and triggers immediate KV cache eviction for that session to free resources. 2) Disconnect / reconnect & resume: Add a resumable streaming handshake that issues a short-lived resume_token in the final event of a partial stream (or on explicit checkpoint). Clients that reconnect with the resume_token and matching session_id will receive a resume delta if the server still has cached state. Resume window is configurable (default 30s). 3) Server-side idle and request timeouts: Add configurable timeouts to auto-close abandoned streams and surface clear error codes to clients and to the OpenAI compatibility layer. Default conservative values chosen, can be tuned by deployment. 4) OpenAI-compat updates: Map new lifecycle semantics to OpenAI-compatible HTTP streaming (SSE/chunked) and introduce compatible headers x-rwd-resume-token and x-rwd-session-id so existing OpenAI clients can opt-in without breaking older clients. 5) Telemetry & metrics: Add streaming.session_active_seconds, streaming.resume_attempts, streaming.resume_success, streaming.client_cancels counters and traces to help SRE and customers reason about lifecycle events. 6) Tests & docs: Add unit tests for the state machine, integration tests simulating reconnect/resume, and update API docs and examples. Implementation notes: - Runtime: Add StreamLifecycleManager that tracks ephemeral sessions, tokens, expiry, and eviction. Integrates with KV cache to allow quick resume of prefix state. - API Layer: New headers and wire events implemented in openai-compat proxy and native API handlers. - Backpressure: Keep existing batching/backpressure behavior; resume replays only the minimal suffix needed to continue generation. - Security: Resume tokens are opaque HMACed blobs with expiry. No persistent PII stored. - Opt-in behavior: Resume is off by default for older clients; availability is advertised through the info frame on connection. Compatibility: This is designed to be backwards compatible. Older clients that do not use resume_token see no change other than clearer error codes on timeouts. Deploy strategy: Feature-flag gated rollout with Canary (10% traffic) -> 50% -> 100% with a kill-switch. Linear tickets: ENG-7643 (design + tracking), ENG-7721 (OpenAI compat adjustments).
